chapter: Capone's Chicago, the union and hired by Cab
title: Working in Capone-run clubs: Boyd Atkins, Ed Depappa and mean Ralph Capone
summary: Hinton lists Capone-family clubs that used all-black entertainment, with Boyd Atkins's band, and contrasts brutal Ralph with Al, whom he calls a nice man to work for.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Who were some of the other people you worked with? Now you worked with Eddie. Who else did you work with in Chicago?
Well I worked with Boyd Atkins.

Yeah, Boyd Atkins. Al Capone had the Cotton Club on Cicero and then they begin to branch out. This guy Ed Depappa had the club where… a small club on the north side where Eddie South was. And Ralph Capone, Al Capone‟s brother opened a club downtown in Chicago.
Yeah, and they made it all black entertainment. But Ralph was an animal. He was really mean.

Oh, he was just absolutely terrible. Al was a nice guy that we could work for. My uncle worked for him. Let me tell you about that too a little later. That‟s where I got all these scars on me, working for Al Capone. That‟s right.
